newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine water firm asked to speed up expansion.
newsitem.headline: Argentine water firm asked to speed up expansion.

text.p: The Argentine government has asked water company Aguas Argentinas, controlled by France's Lyonnaise des Eaux to accelerate the expansion of its sewer network, a top official of the Argentine company said Friday.
"The government started negotiations for us to speed-up our expansion plans," the official, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters.
"The expansion was included in the original contract and envisaged for the next 10 years but they are asking us to accelerate it."
Aguas Argentinas took over the concession on water services in Buenos Aires and sorrounding areas in 1993 after the privatization of the former state company Obras Sanitarias de la Nacion.
A decree signed by President Carlos Menem Thursday allowed the modification of the contract with Aguas Argentinas in order to start negotiations.
The official said the government wanted the firm to accelerate the expansion in the Matanza-Riachuelo area, in Buenos Aires Province, one of the country's most densely populated.
He added one of the main issues will be an infrastructure payment the company stopped charging clients last year at the government's request.
"That means an annual negative impact for the company in the range of $40 to $50 million," the official said. "We hope this issue will be solved."
The official said since 1993 the company has invested $800 million, exceeding what was agreed in the concession agreement.
Separately, a consortium headed by Lyonnaise is the sole bidder in a water services concession in the central Province of Cordoba.
